name: Moltis
vibe_summary: A security-first personal agent server written in Rust, shipping as a single sandboxed binary with multi-provider LLMs, voice, memory, and chat integrations. It positions itself as the hardened, auditable alternative to OpenClaw's TypeScript stack.
best_for: Security-conscious users wanting sandboxed agent execution
Self-hosters on low-power hardware like Raspberry Pi
Rust developers who want an auditable agent codebase
avoid_if: You need a mature plugin marketplace or large skill ecosystem
You want mobile companion apps out of the box
You prefer a larger, more established community
You need extensive third-party documentation and tutorials
openclaw_advantages: Single Rust binary with no Node.js runtime dependency
Sandboxed container execution for every command by default
Smaller auditable core (~7.5K lines for agent runner and model interface)
Lower memory footprint suitable for Raspberry Pi-class hardware
No plugin marketplace, reducing supply-chain attack surface
openclaw_disadvantages: Smaller community and ecosystem than OpenClaw
Younger project with less production battle-testing
Ecosystem digests have flagged it as early-stage or inconsistently active

overview_markdown:
Moltis is a secure, persistent personal agent server written entirely in Rust, distributed as a single self-contained binary with no Node.js or npm runtime dependencies. Its core differentiator is a security-first architecture: every command executes inside a sandboxed container rather than on the host, API keys never leave the local machine, and unsafe code is isolated to FFI and precompiled runtime boundaries. The workspace spans ~270K lines across 59 modular crates, but the agent runner and model interface fit in roughly 7.5K auditable lines, with 470+ test files.

Feature-wise it is surprisingly complete: multi-provider LLM support, voice, cross-session memory and recall, automatic edit checkpoints, scheduling, Telegram/Signal/Discord/WhatsApp/Teams integrations, browser automation, MCP server support, SSH or node-backed remote execution, and managed deploy keys with host pinning. It deliberately avoids a plugin marketplace, framing that as a supply-chain security win rather than a limitation.

Compared to OpenClaw's TypeScript stack with Swift/Kotlin companion apps, Moltis trades ecosystem breadth for auditability, a minimal footprint, and hardened defaults. It runs comfortably on a Mac Mini or Raspberry Pi, installs via a one-liner, Homebrew, Docker, or cargo, and recently hit the Hacker News front page. Recent commits show active release engineering, including macOS notarization hardening and frequent dated releases.
